text.p: Shares in French drinks company Pernod Ricard lost their fizz on Thursday, shedding 2.46 percent to 320.90 francs on volume of 66,714 shares at 1240 GMT.
Market sources said the fall was due to profit-taking after the 1996 results, which were in line with estimates, and the company's cautious outlook for 1997. The stock had risen in the last few days.

However, Goldman Sachs upped its rating on the stock to market outperformer from market performer, while Cholet-Dupont upgraded it to accumulate from lighten. The French broker also raised its earnings estimate for Pernod.

Cholet-Dupont revised its 1997 net earnings per share estimate to 22.1 francs from 21.2 and held the 1998 estimate at 23.4 francs. It said the company would benefit from lower financial costs and had softened the impact of overstocking.
Pernod reported 1996 net attributable profit of 1.19 billion francs and said 1997 would be characterised by overstocking in France in wines and spirits at the end of 1996.
